title: Max Sum of Subarray Size K
statement: Write `max_sum_subarray(arr, k)` that returns the maximum sum of any contiguous subarray of length `k`.

predict_steps.prompt: First window [2,1,5] sums to 8. When sliding right, which value leaves?
After leaving 2 and adding 1, what is the new window sum?

learn_quiz.question: Brute force per window is roughly?

viva.question: Why is a fixed window of size k linear instead of rebuilding each window sum?
expected_points: sliding removes the leaving element and adds the entering one
each element enters and leaves the window at most once
total work stays linear in the array length
restarting the sum from scratch each time would be quadratic

viva.question: What breaks when n is smaller than k?
expected_points: no window of length k exists
the algorithm must treat that as invalid or empty per the statement
blindly indexing k steps ahead would go out of range
the first full window cannot be formed

viva.question: Why does subtracting the leaving element keep the running sum correct?
expected_points: window membership changes by exactly one index on each slide
the old left value is no longer inside the window
the new right value is the only addition
the invariant is that the running sum equals the current window contents
